title: Human vs. AI: Who Can You Trust?
description: A 75-minute interactive Week 08 evidence lab that prepares students for the Gen Ed Signature Assignment: Analyzing AI & Human Decision-Making.

steps.label: ARRIVAL
steps.title: Human vs. AI: Who Can You Trust?
steps.lead: Today you are not here to memorize AI ethics. You are here to investigate claims, evidence, and human behavior.
steps.studentTask: Join on your phone. Then look up.

runbook.openWith: I missed you last week, so today we are going to make Week 08 count.
runbook.whyMatters: Frames the class as an investigation that directly produces material for the Gen Ed Signature Assignment.
runbook.landHere: Your job today is to decide what the evidence actually supports.
runbook.transition: First: would you follow the AI?

steps.label: TRUST TEST
steps.title: AI says you are a poor fit for a job. Would you follow the recommendation?
steps.lead: Make your own call before you hear anyone else.
steps.studentTask: Vote first. Then be ready to explain what information you would want before acting.
steps.roomInstruction: TRUST IT · CHECK IT · IGNORE IT
steps.visualCaption: What would make you trust this recommendation?

runbook.openWith: No discussion yet. Commit to your first instinct.
runbook.whyMatters: Surfaces students' implicit standards for trust before formalizing evidence-based reasoning.
runbook.ask: What information would you need before acting on the recommendation?
runbook.pause: 30 seconds to vote, then 2–3 fast explanations.
runbook.listenFor: Accuracy, data source, bias, stakes, who made the system, whether a human reviewed it.
runbook.ifTheySay: I would never trust AI → ask whether they use recommendations in maps, shopping, music, or search.
runbook.ifQuiet: Ask: would your answer change if the recommendation affected only what movie you watched?
runbook.pushFurther: What changes when the consequence is a job opportunity?
runbook.revealWhen: Most of the room has voted.
runbook.sayDuringReveal: Notice that your trust standard changes with consequence.
runbook.landHere: Trust is not one setting. Context and consequence change the burden of evidence.
runbook.transition: Now let’s see whether we can tell evidence from vibes.

steps.label: EVIDENCE OR VIBES · 1
steps.title: “People trust AI too much.”
steps.lead: Is this evidence, or is it only a claim?
steps.studentTask: Classify the statement. Then explain what would turn it into evidence.
steps.visualCaption: What would you need to see?

runbook.openWith: This sentence sounds plausible. Plausible is not the same as supported.
runbook.whyMatters: Introduces the difference between opinion and empirical support.
runbook.ask: What would researchers have to observe or measure to support this claim?
runbook.listenFor: Surveys, experiments, observed choices, comparison groups, before/after behavior.
runbook.ifTheySay: It is evidence because it sounds true → ask where the data is.
runbook.ifQuiet: Ask: who are 'people'? Trust which AI? In what decision?
runbook.pushFurther: How would you define 'trust too much' in something measurable?
runbook.landHere: A claim becomes researchable when we define the people, behavior, evidence, and context.
runbook.transition: Now I’m going to give you a stronger claim.

steps.label: EVIDENCE OR VIBES · 2
steps.title: “In a study, participants followed AI advice more often when it was presented with high confidence.”
steps.lead: Does this sentence give us enough to make a conclusion?
steps.studentTask: Choose the best classification. Be ready to say what the sentence still does not prove.

runbook.openWith: This is much stronger than 'people trust AI too much'—but it still has limits.
runbook.ask: What can we reasonably say? What can we NOT say?
runbook.pause: Vote, then call on one student for each side.
runbook.listenFor: This study/context only; participants may not represent everyone; confidence may influence behavior but does not prove causation unless design supports it.
runbook.ifTheySay: This proves AI manipulates people → ask what the study actually measured.
runbook.ifQuiet: Ask whether one study lets us say 'everyone always does this.'
runbook.pushFurther: What detail about the method would increase your confidence?
runbook.landHere: Evidence earns a bounded conclusion—not a bigger one than the method supports.
runbook.transition: Now you become the research team.

steps.label: DETECTIVE BRIEF
steps.title: AI Behavior Detective
steps.lead: Your team will investigate one human + AI decision case.
steps.studentTask: Form a team of 3–4. Choose one case category from the Signature Assignment.
steps.roomInstruction: CASE → CONTEXT → EVIDENCE → HUMAN BEHAVIOR → FINDINGS → LIMITS
steps.visualCaption: Use the case/source you will analyze for the Signature Assignment.

runbook.openWith: For the next 15 minutes, you are not students. You are the evidence team.
runbook.whyMatters: Directly mirrors the Signature Assignment structure.
runbook.ask: Choose a case category and open a credible case, study, report, or data-based source connected to it.
runbook.pause: Give teams time to form and choose.
runbook.listenFor: Students choosing something specific enough to analyze.
runbook.ifTheySay: Can we just use an AI summary? → no; they need a source with evidence about human behavior.
runbook.ifQuiet: Assign categories by table if choosing takes too long.
runbook.landHere: Your job is not to decide whether AI is good or bad. Your job is to explain what the evidence shows about people interacting with AI.
runbook.transition: Open the case. Start the investigation.

steps.label: CASE INVESTIGATION
steps.title: Build the Evidence Board
steps.lead: Find the pieces your Signature Assignment needs.
choices: AI CONTEXT — What system or process is involved?
HUMAN BEHAVIOR — What are people doing, trusting, resisting, or deciding?
EVIDENCE — What was gathered or measured?
METHOD — How was the evidence gathered or analyzed?
steps.studentTask: As a team, identify: AI context, people, behavior, evidence, method, finding, and one limit. Write down your answers.
steps.roomInstruction: SOLVE THE CASE · DO NOT JUST SUMMARIZE IT
steps.visualCaption: Ask: What does the evidence show? What does it NOT show?

runbook.openWith: The assignment gets easier when you stop reading for topic and start reading for evidence.
runbook.whyMatters: Students practice the exact D3 evidence analysis required by the Signature Assignment.
runbook.ask: What behavior did the source actually observe or measure?
runbook.pause: 15-minute team investigation. Circulate rather than lecture.
runbook.listenFor: Specific methods, measures, behaviors, findings, limitations.
runbook.ifTheySay: The evidence is 'the article' → ask what data or observations the article is reporting.
runbook.ifQuiet: Ask each team: what is one thing your source can support and one thing it cannot?
runbook.pushFurther: What would make this evidence stronger?
runbook.landHere: A strong analysis connects method → evidence → behavior → finding → reasonable implication.
runbook.transition: Now let AI try to overstate your evidence.

steps.label: CONFIDENCE TRAP
steps.title: Catch the AI Overclaim
steps.lead: Ask AI what your evidence proves. Your job is to catch it overstating the case.
steps.studentTask: Ask AI: “What does this evidence prove about human behavior with AI?” Find one sentence that is stretched, unsupported, or too broad. Submit the sentence or your correction.
steps.visualCaption: AI can summarize evidence and still overstate what it means.

runbook.openWith: Now I want you to make AI do something dangerous: sound certain.
runbook.whyMatters: Turns AI-use documentation and verification into an authentic activity.
runbook.ask: Which sentence goes farther than the evidence allows?
runbook.pause: Teams challenge AI, then each student submits one overclaim or corrected version.
runbook.listenFor: Always, proves, causes, everyone, never, definitive claims unsupported by sample/method.
runbook.ifTheySay: The AI answer looks fine → ask them to circle the strongest verb in the answer.
runbook.ifQuiet: Tell them to search for 'proves,' 'causes,' 'always,' 'everyone,' or missing context.
runbook.pushFurther: How would you rewrite the sentence so the claim matches the evidence?
runbook.revealWhen: At least several responses are in; reveal a few anonymously.
runbook.sayDuringReveal: Fluent language can hide an evidence problem.
runbook.transition: Time to put claims on trial.

steps.label: EVIDENCE COURT
steps.title: Put Your Claim on Trial
steps.lead: Your team gets 30 seconds. The room gets to challenge the evidence.
steps.studentTask: Submit your team's best one-sentence claim: “Our evidence suggests ______.” Then be ready to defend it.

runbook.openWith: Welcome to Evidence Court. Every team gets one claim. The rest of us get to challenge it.
runbook.whyMatters: Students practice defending a bounded evidence-based conclusion in public.
runbook.ask: What evidence supports that? Are they claiming more than the source shows?
runbook.pause: 30 seconds per selected team. Keep pace fast.
runbook.listenFor: Specific source evidence, limits, method, reasonable implications.
runbook.ifTheySay: That's just obvious → ask what the source actually measured.
runbook.ifQuiet: Use the first submitted claim and ask the room to vote verbally: supported, needs evidence, or too far.
runbook.pushFurther: What single word would you change to make the claim more defensible?
runbook.revealWhen: Reveal submitted claims and choose 3–4 for rapid challenge.
runbook.landHere: Good evidence reasoning includes both what you can say and what you should not say.
runbook.transition: Everything you just did is the hardest part of your Signature Assignment.

steps.label: SIGNATURE BUILD
steps.title: Turn the Investigation Into Your Assignment
steps.lead: Start the 80-point Gen Ed Signature Assignment while the evidence is fresh.
steps.studentTask: Individually draft the first four sections: source/case overview, context, evidence/method, and human behavior. Use your team work, but write your own analysis.
steps.roomInstruction: START THE REAL ASSIGNMENT · ASK FOR HELP NOW

runbook.openWith: You have already done the thinking. Now capture it while I am here to help.
runbook.whyMatters: Converts engagement into progress on the high-value Gen Ed artifact.
runbook.ask: Where are you stuck: case, method, behavior, finding, or limit?
runbook.pause: 12 minutes of quiet individual work. Circulate.
runbook.listenFor: Students confusing findings with implications or source summary with evidence method.
runbook.ifTheySay: Can AI write this? → AI can help challenge or organize, but the interpretation and final judgment must be theirs and documented.
runbook.landHere: Your assignment should make your reasoning visible from evidence to conclusion.
runbook.transition: One final test before you leave.

steps.label: FINAL BOSS
steps.title: Which TWO questions protect you from an evidence overclaim?
steps.lead: Pick the two that matter most before you make a strong conclusion.
choices: WHAT DOES THE EVIDENCE ACTUALLY SHOW?
WHAT DOES THE EVIDENCE NOT SHOW?
DO I PERSONALLY AGREE WITH THE RESULT?
steps.studentTask: Choose exactly two. Lock them in.

runbook.openWith: Last question. This one is the entire week in miniature.
runbook.whyMatters: Ends on the central D3 reasoning habit.
runbook.ask: Which two questions keep us from claiming more than our evidence supports?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: These two questions are the difference between evidence-based reasoning and vibes.
runbook.landHere: AI can make a claim. Evidence earns the conclusion.
runbook.transition: Save your case and your notes. You have already started the Signature Assignment.
